one_line: Recent developments cover privacy issues in developer tools, major security acquisitions, new open-weight world simulation models, and methods to improve LLM inference reproducibility and reinforcement learning efficiency.

stories.title: Claude Code Sends User Email Addresses to Websites
stories.summary: Claude Code has been observed sending user email addresses to external websites. This privacy leak was documented in a recent GitHub issue.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers using Claude Code should be aware that their email addresses may be transmitted to external sites during operation.
stories.editor_reason: Claude Code leaks user email addresses to websites, sparking major security concerns.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks in Talks to Acquire Clutch Security for $500M
stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to acquire Clutch Security for $500 million in cash plus milestone payouts. If completed, this would mark Palo Alto Networks' seventh acquisition of the year.
stories.why_it_matters: This potential cash and milestone deal would represent Palo Alto Networks' seventh acquisition of the year, expanding its corporate portfolio.
stories.editor_reason: Palo Alto Networks in talks to acquire AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M.

facts.claim: Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to acquire Clutch Security for $500 million in cash plus milestone payouts.
facts.quote: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security, a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts

facts.claim: If completed, this would mark Palo Alto Networks' seventh acquisition of the year.
facts.quote: If the deal happens, it would be Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition this year, according to PitchBook.

first_issues.problem: The facts do not state that Clutch Security is an AI agent security startup.

stories.title: NVIDIA Releases Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
stories.summary: NVIDIA released four new open-weight checkpoints for its Cosmos 3 model family, featuring 16 billion trainable parameters for interactive world simulation and driving scene generation. The models are released under the OpenMDW1.1 license, which permits commercial and non-commercial use.
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers and developers gain new openly licensed, high-parameter models for building interactive world simulations and driving scenes.
stories.editor_reason: NVIDIA releases Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation.

facts.claim: NVIDIA released four new open-weight checkpoints for its Cosmos 3 model family to enable interactive world simulation and driving scene generation.
facts.quote: NVIDIA Cosmos world model development platform adds four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family for generating interactive world simulation

facts.claim: The new models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and feature 16 billion trainable parameters.
facts.quote: All four models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and have 16B trainable parameters.

facts.claim: The models are released under OpenMDW1.1, which permits both commercial and non-commercial use.
facts.quote: The models use OpenMDW1.1, permitting commercial and non-commercial use under its terms.

facts.claim: The four specific models added are Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer, and Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual.
facts.quote:
- 🌦️ Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto : Generate multi-view driving data with varied weather, lighting, and time of day.
- 🚗 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto : Stream synchronized camera and LiDAR observations for driving simulation.
- 🎨 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer : Turn simulator controls and a text prompt into photorealistic video.
- 🤖 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual : Predict video from robot or camera actions.

stories.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
stories.summary: BlockLock is a new method for reproducible LLM inference that fixes request geometry to ensure identical outputs regardless of batch changes. It operates in two modes, BlockLock-Rows and BlockLock-Pack, both preserving target outputs bitwise under a per-deployment contract.
stories.why_it_matters: You can use BlockLock to guarantee bitwise-identical LLM inference outputs despite changes in batch composition.
stories.editor_reason: New 'BlockLock' technique enables reproducible LLM inference with fixed batch geometry.

facts.claim: BlockLock is introduced as a method for reproducible LLM inference that fixes request geometry to ensure identical outputs regardless of batch changes.
facts.quote: We present BlockLock, which keeps shared batched prefill and pins only the numerical path of the protected request

facts.claim: BlockLock operates in two modes: BlockLock-Rows and BlockLock-Pack, both of which preserve the target's output bitwise under a stated per-deployment contract.
facts.quote: Both modes preserve the target's output bitwise when its companions change.

stories.title: FlexFloor Improves Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training
stories.summary: FlexFloor is a new system designed to enable earlier resource release during synchronous response generation in mixture-of-experts models by using historical response lengths and memory constraints. It increases response generation throughput by 52.74% and generates about 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time compared to the baseline.
stories.why_it_matters: Implementing FlexFloor reduces wasted worker time during mixture-of-experts model training, significantly boosting generation throughput.
stories.editor_reason: Elastic Expert Parallelism improves resource efficiency in LLM reinforcement learning post-training.

facts.claim: Approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline is wasted because workers remain occupied waiting for other experts to finish processing longer responses.
facts.quote: approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes

facts.claim: FlexFloor is introduced as a new system designed to enable earlier resource release during synchronous response generation in mixture-of-experts models.
facts.quote: Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses.

facts.claim: FlexFloor uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to manage batching and prompt placement while progressively releasing workers.
facts.quote: It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication.

facts.claim: FlexFloor generates about 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time compared to the verl baseline.
facts.quote: Compared with the verl baseline, FlexFloor generates approximately 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time

facts.claim: FlexFloor increases response generation throughput by 52.74% with little observed variation in rollout reward.
facts.quote: increases response generation throughput by 52.74%, with little observed variation in rollout reward.
